The includes receiver is a normalized path string, not an array. It detects the /node_modules/ path segment in compiler-resolved declaration filenames. A Set membership test would not test substring containment.
The includes call matches a substring of the normalized physical path, rather than searching an array of paths. Segment locality determines which third-party declarations are eligible.

TypeScript lib reference directives are exceptional; the lookup takes the first matching basename in compiler source order. Building another full index would also require preserving first-match behavior for duplicate basenames.

The builder first asks TypeScript which declarations are default libraries, then maps only those paths to their virtual URLs. This is a build-time linear selection, not repeated traversal of declarations at runtime.

Loader aliases only exist when public and resolved leaf specifiers differ. Selecting them before producing alias tuples keeps canonical loaders separate and occurs only when emitting the virtual module.
The entries iterator is materialized for sort; it is not an existing array for which toSorted would avoid a copy. The sorted export map makes the generated module deterministic.

The static document generator replaces matching style tags in the accumulating markup. The ordered build-only replacements bound minifier concurrency and preserve the CSS association and order in the served motion document.

The emitted inventory first selects scenario-owned chunks or typed bundle assets, then maps filenames and sorts them. The static closure must exclude merely lazy resources, while recording the actual emitted assets deterministically.
id.includes tests whether a single Rollup module ID contains the native declarations virtual ID; equality against a Set cannot replace the substring check.
The virtual runtime emits aliases only for differing module and canonical loader specifiers. A linear filter then tuple projection keeps aliases and actual lazy loaders separate in generated code.

The output hook scans emitted chunks once for the fallback hero root then extracts those filenames. Discovery hints must not pull the full authenticated or motion document runtime onto the fallback path.

The test evaluates the checked-in generator’s own synthetic output after replacing indexed Rollup placeholders with fixture URLs. This executes neither product input nor remotely supplied code; it verifies the emitted index contract.
This test executes only the declaration index module emitted from controlled in-memory inputs. The assertion verifies generated URL and hash values as JavaScript, not a production evaluation path.

Serial traversal and sidecar compression cap outstanding buffers and maximum-quality Brotli jobs during a build. Parallelizing across output files would increase peak memory without changing the emitted sidecar contract.

The production bundle hook projects stable manifest filenames before selecting shell-locale files. This is a single bounded build pass; preload membership is the relevant contract, not callback fusion.

HTML hints can include a base prefix, so the lookup resolves a bundle filename by pathname suffix. Indexing by the full URL would miss prefixed document assets; the one-time build check validates their byte cost.
The build checker selects static sign-in roots before projecting filenames, and the failure path selects chunks before formatting contributors. Neither operates in a browser render path.
The resource collection is a Set of required and speculatively discovered files; the spread materializes it for deterministic ordering. Switching to toSorted would still require materialization.
